title: Filter cache
description:
Filter results can be cached. If a filter was used previously and the cache
has a match an entire rescan can prevented and instead the filtered packet list
can be restored from the cache. The cache is limited to be used with capture
files.

If a filter result is restored from the cache instead of rescanning the file
the user gets a temporary message shown in the statusbar.

The maximum size of the cache can be customized by the user via prefenrence.
The cache is can be disabled by by setting the maximum size to 0.
By default the cache is disabled.

notes.body:
added 10 commits
  • d340ab9f...0ca960c6 - 9 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 67110924 - Filter cache
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7638/diffs?diff_id=453534268&start_sha=d340ab9fb8611be4d2b7b5a5d43a9532dfd6275c)

You would also have to take into account, that the cache can become invalid due to a variety of other reasons as well:

* Name resolution changed
* GeoIP has been enabled/disabled
* Preferences of protocols have been changed (think TLS key added which now decrypts)
* Preferences for name resolution have changed
* Profile has changed

That being said, I think this could be a very cool thing to add, but the above items should be adressed.

> You would also have to take into account, that the cache can become invalid due to a variety of other reasons as well

Anything that forces a redissection of the packets also must force a flushing of the cache.
Agreed, might be the easier route to go, all of the things above should force a redissection anyway.
How to proceed? Is there something missing for this MR to be merged?

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7638/diffs?diff_id=453814161&start_sha=6711092418753627a5b65e9d8adb5066b78b2815)
Closed as it doesn't seem to be of any interest.

I would like to revive some of my old ideas and wonder if this feature has a chance to make it into one of the next releases?

It would be a significant improvement of my workflow with a decent boost of productivity.

Overall I like the idea. Along with quickly switching between display filters it might be useful to cache column sort orders and even add multiple packet list views, e.g. via tabs or separate windows. I'll add some specific comments shortly.
Having multiple packet list views via tabs would be even an even better solution from my point of view. But that would make this MR obsolete.

As discussed in !10517 I'd prefer to keep the main preference panes as simple as possible. We should probably come up with a default that's good enough for most people and leave this as an advanced preference, otherwise we'll end up with an [airliner cockpit](https://www.airbus.com/en/products-services/commercial-aircraft/cockpits).
I am ok with that. So i will move it to advanced settings.
I think this is useful for testing, but it gets annoying pretty quickly. Maybe only enable it if the log level is debug or noisy?
I thought it could be useful for the user as well since he might wonder why filtering sometimes takes some time and sometime it goes very quickly.

[commenting in the right place this time]

I think this should be enabled, particularly if we can get this merged in time to shake out bugs before the next major release. Also, should this be a memory size instead of a count?

I think it will be hard for the user to determine how much memory would be required if he wants a history of 10 entries. (for example)

On the other hand it is more predictable if you want to prevent filter entries of flooding your memory. But I think you would need to apply many different filters to get to that point.

I would assume having a default of 10 or 15 (filters) would work fine for most people.
